one_line: A synthetic, hand-authored fixture: adding three steps of observation history lifts held-out success from 0.64 to 0.72, and an auxiliary prediction loss adds another 0.03; moving the same recipe from GPU-A to GPU-B changes nothing beyond seed noise.
background: All numbers in this example are hand-authored fixtures written to demonstrate LabWeft; no training was executed. The toy study asks how much a small policy benefits from seeing recent observations, whether an auxiliary next-observation prediction objective helps on top of that, and whether a hardware change needs a new ablation.

method.name: History-conditioned policy with an auxiliary prediction loss
method.idea: Encode the last k observations instead of the current one only, and optionally add a weighted next-observation prediction loss. Every condition is trained for 20k steps on toy-v1 and evaluated with the held-out protocol heldout-v1, three training seeds each.

components.name: HistoryEncoder (history_length)
components.role: Keeps the last k observations; k = 0 reduces to the current observation only.

components.name: Auxiliary prediction objective (prediction_weight)
components.role: Weighted squared error on predicted next observations; 0 disables it.

components.name: Fixed protocol
components.role: toy-v1 data, fp32, 20k steps, heldout-v1 evaluation, seeds 0/1/2.

glossary.meaning: Fraction of held-out episodes solved (0 to 1).
The four recorded conditions; each folder name ends in its training seed.

phases.title: Baseline without history
phases.summary: C0 trains the policy on the current observation only (history_length 0) and sets the reference: 0.64 ± 0.01 over three seeds.

phases.title: Add three steps of history
phases.summary: C1 changes only history_length to 3; success rises to 0.72 ± 0.01 on every seed.

phases.title: Auxiliary prediction on top of history
phases.summary: C2 keeps history and sets prediction_weight 0.1; success reaches 0.75 ± 0.01.

phases.title: Same recipe on GPU-B
phases.summary: C3 repeats C2 on GPU-B; 0.74 ± 0.01 overlaps C2, and the researcher's note scopes when the hardware judgment may be reused.

claims.statement: Three steps of observation history improve held-out success from 0.64 to 0.72 (three seeds each, same data, steps and protocol).

numbers.meaning: C0, no history, mean ± SD over seeds
C1, history_length 3, mean ± SD over seeds

claims.caveats: Synthetic fixture; toy-v1 data and heldout-v1 protocol only.

claims.statement: With history enabled, an auxiliary prediction loss (weight 0.1) adds a further 0.03 of success.
claims.caveats: One weight tested; the dose-response is unknown.

claims.statement: Moving the C2 recipe from GPU-A to GPU-B does not change success beyond seed noise, so a new hardware-only ablation is not needed under the recorded scope.
claims.caveats: Three seeds do not establish equivalence; reopen if implementation, precision, data, budget or protocol change.

experiments.question: Does seeing recent observations help the policy?
experiments.finding: History helps on every seed: +0.08 absolute success.

experiments.question: Does an auxiliary prediction loss add anything once history is on?
experiments.finding: A small, consistent gain of 0.03; only one weight was tried.

experiments.question: Does the same recipe behave the same on different hardware?
experiments.finding: Within seed noise; the researcher accepts reusing the hardware judgment for this recorded scope only.

invalidated.what: Re-running the hardware-only ablation for every new training seed
invalidated.why: A new seed is replication, not a new hardware condition.
invalidated.replaced_by: Reopen the hardware question only if implementation, precision, data, budget or protocol change.

open_questions.question: How does success change with other prediction weights (0.03, 0.3)?
Does the history gain hold beyond three steps or on a second dataset?
